stem: During a routine newborn hip screening examination, which finding most clearly requires referral for possible developmental dysplasia of the hip?

options.A: A positive Ortolani maneuver with a palpable hip clunk
options.B: Symmetric spontaneous movement of both lower extremities
options.C: A soft, painless hip click without instability
options.D: Symmetric gluteal folds with full passive hip motion

rationale: AAP guidance identifies an unstable or dislocated hip with a positive Ortolani test as a primary indication for referral in infancy. A soft hip click without instability is not equivalent to an Ortolani clunk, and symmetric movement/folds with unrestricted motion are reassuring findings. Limited or asymmetric abduction becomes a more useful referral finding after the neonatal period, so it was not mixed into this newborn-specific item. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Recognize a positive Ortolani maneuver as a concerning newborn screening finding for developmental dysplasia of the hip that warrants referral.
source_document_title: Evaluation and Referral for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip in Infants
source_version_date: AAP Clinical Report, Pediatrics 2016; current AAP publication accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Clinical Examination: Ortolani maneuver is the most important clinical test for detecting newborn dysplasia; Referral section: primary indications include an unstable (positive Ortolani) or dislocated hip; limited/asymmetric abduction after the neonatal period is also a referral indication
source_claim_supported: A positive Ortolani maneuver in an infant indicates a dislocated/reducible unstable hip and is a primary indication for referral for DDH evaluation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — growth and development, newborn/infant assessment, screening and early identification of health problems
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — newborn developmental screening / developmental dysplasia of the hip
correction_summary: Removed the source item's age-mixed cluster of gluteal-fold asymmetry, limited abduction, and Ortolani/Barlow findings. Rebuilt the question around the newborn-specific positive Ortolani referral finding and corrected the blueprint from Physiological Adaptation to Health Promotion and Maintenance.
audit_findings: A is the strongest AAP-supported newborn referral finding. B and D are reassuring. C deliberately distinguishes a benign click from a true Ortolani clunk/instability. Barlow was not used as the key because many newborn Barlow-positive hips stabilize and are followed serially. No second answer, age ambiguity, cueing, or unresolved blueprint conflict remains. Independent adversarial second pass passed.
